note: The fuzzer passes the raw DNS packet bytes and their length to the DNS protocol decode test point.
The DNS decode context stores the start of the attacker-controlled packet for later compressed-label parsing.

code: slen = decode_record(ctx, cursor, attr_dns_rr, p, end - p, packet_ctx, packet + 6);
note: The answer count field selects RR decoding over the bytes after the DNS header.

code: slen = fr_struct_from_network(ctx, cursor, attr, p, end - p, true, packet_ctx, decode_value_trampoline, NULL);
note: The resource record body is parsed as a DNS RR structure.

code: slen = fr_dns_label_uncompressed_length(packet_ctx->packet, data, data + data_len - packet_ctx->packet, &next, packet_ctx->lb);
note: The code computes the label buffer length from data + data_len - packet start, so for RR RDATA this length is larger than the actual one-byte RDATA field.
The oversized length creates an end pointer beyond the allocated input buffer.
The malformed RDATA begins with length byte 1; the oversized end makes the one-byte label appear in bounds.
The label verifier reads q at one byte past the supplied fuzz input while validating the nonexistent label character.
